title: Measuring Cellular Energetics via Noncanonical Amino Acid Tagging in Immune Cells
author: Vrieling, van der Zande, et al.
materials:
Timing: variable
Note: Recipes for required solutions are detailed under materials and equipment.
1.Prepare solutions, buffers and stocks required for immune cell isolation:a.Peritoneal lavage buffer.b.Krebs buffer.c.HEPES stock.d.HEPES-buffered Krebs solution.e.Collagenase D stock.f.DNAse I stock.g.eWAT digestion buffer.h.Liver digestion buffer.i.Spleen digestion buffer.j.Kidney/lung digestion buffer.k.Wash buffer.l.RBC lysis buffer.2.Prepare solutions, buffers and stocks required for CENCAT:a.Complete RPMI1640 medium.b.2-DG stock.c.Oligomycin stock.d.βES stock.e.Cu(II)SO4 stock.f.THPTA stock.g.AZDye Azide Plus stock.h.Permeabilization buffer.i.Click buffer.j.FACS buffer.

steps.title: Prepare isolation buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare all solutions, buffers, and stocks required for immune cell isolation as listed (peritoneal lavage buffer, Krebs buffer, HEPES stock, HEPES‑buffered Krebs solution, Collagenase D stock, DNAse I stock, eWAT digestion buffer, liver digestion buffer, spleen digestion buffer, kidney/lung digestion buffer, wash buffer, RBC lysis buffer) according to the recipes in the Materials and Equipment section.

steps.title: Prepare CENCAT reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare all solutions, buffers, and stocks required for CENCAT: complete RPMI‑1640 medium, 2‑DG stock, oligomycin stock, β‑ES stock, Cu(II)SO4 stock, THPTA stock, AZDye Azide Plus stock, permeabilization buffer, click buffer, and FACS buffer, following the detailed recipes provided.

steps.title: Isolate and activate PBMCs
steps.instruction: Isolate human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from EDTA‑treated blood using Ficoll density centrifugation and wash them as follows.

substeps.instruction: Dilute EDTA blood 1:1 with PBS at 18 °C–20 °C.

Divide the diluted blood among Leucosep tubes containing Ficoll Paque‑Plus; hold each tube at a 45° angle and pipette the blood against the side of the tube (do not pipette directly onto the porous barrier).
Centrifuge the Leucosep tubes at 800 RCF for 15 min at 18 °C–20 °C.
Transfer the top layer (PBMC fraction) to a fresh 50 mL tube by pouring or pipetting.
Add ice‑cold PBS to each tube up to the 50 mL mark and invert the tube three times.
Centrifuge the tubes at 300 RCF for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant by aspiration and gently resuspend the cell pellet.
Optional: pool PBMCs from multiple tubes at this point.
Repeat the washing steps (add PBS, invert, centrifuge) two additional times for a total of three washes.
Count the PBMCs using a hemocytometer or an automated cell counter.

steps.title: Prepare sodium ascorbate stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 19.8 mg sodium ascorbate in 1 mL click buffer to make a 100 mM stock solution; prepare fresh before each use to avoid oxidation.

steps.title: Make click reaction mix
steps.instruction: In click buffer, combine the following components in the order listed, adding sodium ascorbate and AZDye 405 Azide Plus immediately before use: THPTA (200 mM stock, 1:100 dilution → final 2 mM), Cu(II)SO4 (50 mM stock, 1:100 dilution → final 500 µM), sodium ascorbate (100 mM stock, 1:10 dilution → final 10 mM), AZDye 405 Azide Plus (1 µM stock, 1:1000 dilution → final 1 µM).

steps.title: Perform click reaction
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in 100 µL click reaction mix per well, incubate for 30 min at 18 °C–20 °C in the dark, then pellet the cells by centrifugation.

steps.title: Wash post‑click cells
steps.instruction: Wash the pelleted cells with 200 µL FACS buffer and re‑pellet them by centrifugation.

steps.title: Prepare antibody staining mix
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh antibody staining mixes in FACS buffer for (a) human PBMCs and (b) mouse tissue immune cells using the fluorophore‑clone‑dilution pairs listed below; after mixing, centrifuge the antibody mix at 10,000 RCF for 1 min to pellet any aggregates.

substeps.instruction: Human PBMC panel (dilution in parentheses): BUV395 CD14 (MϕP) 1:200, BUV661 HLA‑DR (G46‑61) 1:200, BUV737 CD56 (NCAM) 1:800, Spark Violet 500 CD4 (SK3) 1:400, BV650 CD8 (SK1) 1:200, AlexaFluor 488 CD62L (DREG‑561) 1:200, NovaFluor Blue 610‑70S CD3 (UCHT1) 1:200, PerCPCD45RA (HI) 1:100, PE CD123 (6H61) 1:600, PE‑Cy7 CD11c (S‑HCL‑31) 1:800, APC TCRγ/δ (11F2) 1:400, APC‑R700 CD19 (HIB19) 1:400, APC‑Cy7 CD163 (G81) 1:400, Brilliant Stain Buffer Plus (N/A) 1:10, CellBlox Blocking Buffer (N/A) 1:20.

Mouse tissue panel (dilution in parentheses): FITC CD4 (GK1.5) 1:200, PE TIM‑4 (RMT4‑54) 1:200 (use 1:4000 for peritoneal wash), PE‑Dazzle 594 Siglec‑F (S17007L) 1:100, PerCP‑Cy5.5 CD45 (30‑F111) 1:400, PE‑Cy7 CD8a (53‑6.7) 1:400, APC CD64 (X54‑5/7.1) 1:400, AlexaFluor 700 Ly6C (HK1.4) 1:400, BV510 B220 (RA3‑6B2) 1:100, BV605 CD11c (N418) 1:100, BV650 CD11b (M1/70) 1:800, BV785 MHC‑II (M5/114.15.21) 1:400, Brilliant Stain Buffer Plus (N/A) 1:10.

steps.title: Stain cells with antibodies
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in 50 µL of the appropriate antibody staining mix, incubate for 15 min at 18 °C–20 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Final wash and resuspend
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL FACS buffer to the stained cells, pellet them, then resuspend the final cell suspension at ≤20 × 10⁶ cells/mL.

steps.title: Acquire samples on flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Acquire the samples on a Beckman Coulter CytoFLEX or CytoFLEX LX (or equivalent). Perform instrument quality control using CytoFLEX Ready‑to‑Use Daily QC Fluorospheres (cat# C65719), ensure instrument standardization, and apply proper panel compensation as described in high‑parameter flow cytometry handbooks.

steps.title: Calculate CENCAT parameters
steps.instruction: Using the geometric mean fluorescence intensities (geoMFIs) of ncAA labeling, compute: Mitochondrial dependence (%) = (Vehicle − Oligomycin) / (Vehicle − 2DG + Oligomycin) × 100; Glucose dependence (%) = (Vehicle − 2DG) / (Vehicle − 2DG + Oligomycin) × 100; Glycolytic capacity (%) = 100 − [(Vehicle − Oligomycin) / (Vehicle − 2DG + Oligomycin) × 100]; FAO/AAO capacity (%) = 100 − [(Vehicle − 2DG) / (Vehicle − 2DG + Oligomycin) × 100].

steps.title: Perform PCA analysis
steps.instruction: Mean‑center the CENCAT data and scale to unit standard deviation, then run principal component analysis using the pca() function from the mixOmics R package.

description: This protocol describes the profiling of cellular metabolism using the flow cytometry-based tool CENCAT. We have used this protocol for determining metabolic profiles of naïve and activated human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and murine tissue-resident immune cells from the peritoneal cavity, spleen, epidydimal white adipose tissue, liver, lungs and kidneys.1 This ‘before you begin’ section contains multiple brief workflows for isolating these cells. The isolation procedures are not unique to this protocol and are based on previous work.2,3 However, alternative approaches can also be applied (e.g.4,5,6). Since CENCAT allows the use of any live single cell suspension that can be acquired using flow cytometry, cells from other species, tissues or (non-immune) lineages of interest may be used instead. Finally, given that CENCAT is a flow cytometry-based tool, both homogeneous and heterogeneous suspensions can be metabolically profiled. Experience with multicolor flow cytometry is necessary, yet this falls beyond the scope of this protocol. Design and execution of high parameter flow cytometry have been discussed elsewhere.7 We provide antibody panels for detecting most major immune lineages in human PBMCs and mouse tissues, yet the user may change the panel as desired. However, antibody titration, testing for epitope recognition after formaldehyde fixation and resistance to fluorophore quenching by copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) should be considered when designing an adjusted panel. Of note, different antibody batches and flow cytometer hardware may impact staining resolution. Thus, we recommend the antibody panels shown in this protocol are tested and optimized by the user.
